text: CODEX MASTER PROMPT — EPUBTRANS V2 WEBSITE AUDIT, CORRECTIONS & QUALITY IMPROVEMENT
Act as a senior UI/UX designer, frontend engineer, accessibility specialist, technical SEO engineer, and quality-assurance reviewer working on the EPUBTRANS V2 website.
Project: EPUBTRANS V2 Corporate WebsiteTesting deployment: https://epubtrans-v2.vercel.app/Existing production website: https://www.epubtrans.com/
Your task is to inspect, correct, optimize, and test the existing V2 website based on the approved EPUBTRANS brand standards and the findings listed below.
The objective is to deliver a professional, visually consistent, responsive, accessible, secure, SEO-friendly B2B publishing-services website suitable for international customers.
Important: Improve the existing website. Do not rebuild it unnecessarily, introduce a new design direction, or replace the approved technology stack.
Work only within the EPUBTRANS V2 development repository.
Do not modify, deploy over, or otherwise interfere with the existing production website.
Preserve the approved stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Payload CMS, and PostgreSQL.
Preserve the planned self-hosted production architecture.
Do not introduce unnecessary dependencies, paid services, SaaS platforms, or major architectural changes.
Do not change existing URL slugs without a documented SEO reason and an approved migration decision.
Preserve functioning features, CMS content relationships, and existing user workflows.
Do not invent clients, testimonials, certifications, business statistics, or project outcomes.
Avoid replacing authentic EPUBTRANS portfolio assets with generic stock photographs.
Do not invent privacy policies, legal terms, employment opportunities, or publication permissions.
Inspect actual implementation files and rendered behavior before identifying a defect as confirmed.
Make safe, reversible corrections in logical groups and validate each group.
Do not deploy to production or perform destructive data migrations.
Do not claim a test passed unless it actually ran successfully.
Start by identifying the repository structure, active branch, relevant components, CSS configuration, design tokens, routes, CMS models, and available test commands.
Document the initial findings before changing code, but continue with authorized, low-risk corrections rather than stopping after the audit.
Use these colors as the official design-system baseline.
The screen recording suggested possible differences between the current website colors and the approved brand palette.
These are samples from a compressed recording, not verified CSS values.
Inspect the real CSS, Tailwind configuration, theme variables, computed colors, and component styles.
If the actual implementation uses unauthorized colors, replace them with the appropriate approved design tokens.
Use #F7F9F9 for the main off-white page background.
Preserve intentional white surfaces where appropriate.
Use #078686 as the brand's primary teal.
Use #12383A for dark navigation surfaces, footer backgrounds, and important text where appropriate.
Do not overuse orange, green, or red.
Reserve alert red for error and warning applications where appropriate.
Keep borders, dividers, inputs, and cards visually consistent.

text: The approved primary teal #078686 is slightly below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal-sized white text.
Do not blindly use white text on every brand-teal surface.
Where required, use the smallest practical accessible darkening of the primary teal or another accessible approved foreground/background combination.
Treat any new color variant as a proposed design token requiring owner approval before it becomes a permanent brand-standard change.
Applicable meaningful interface components and state indicators: at least 3:1.
Do not solve contrast problems by redesigning the entire brand.
Create or refine centralized semantic design tokens so the same color meanings remain consistent across components and pages.
Inspect the actual font families, weights, sizes, line heights, letter spacing, and responsive typography.
The approved EPUBTRANS reference does not mandate a particular font family.
Do not replace the current font merely to follow a personal design preference.
Preserve the existing font if it is suitable and consistently implemented.
Establish or refine a maintainable typography token system.
Avoid unnecessary font families and excessive font weights.
Ensure proper Unicode font fallback for Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Bengali, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, and other supported scripts.
Check Arabic right-to-left presentation where supported.
Prevent long headings from overflowing or clipping.
Ensure readable labels, buttons, captions, menus, and form messages.
Avoid excessively small text in cards, dropdown menus, footers, and mobile interfaces.
Suggested typography ranges for evaluation, not mandatory brand specifications:
Prefer consistent typography over arbitrary changes to every element.
Evaluate the hero, introductory content, service categories, industries, capabilities, portfolio, workflow sections, contact CTAs, and footer.
Make the primary message easy to understand within the first screen.
Preserve important SEO content while improving readability.
Establish a clear visual hierarchy between headline, description, supporting information, and CTAs.
Use one visually dominant primary CTA.
Keep secondary actions available but less prominent.
Ensure the hero image supports publishing, localization, accessibility, or content transformation.
Prevent hero images from becoming stretched, pixelated, or excessively large.
Balance the hero at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
Where sections duplicate the same purpose, recommend careful consolidation without losing important business or SEO information.
Do not delete useful content automatically.
Improve section spacing, heading hierarchy, card consistency, and reading flow.
Inspect the desktop header, all mega-menus, the mobile navigation, language selector, and sticky-header behavior.
An issue observed in the desktop recording was that the dark mega-menu could visually blend into the dark footer behind it.
Improve visual separation between open mega-menus and underlying page content.
Ensure dropdown boundaries are visually obvious.
Use consistent column widths, padding, and link spacing.
Verify that menu items have clear hierarchy.
Eliminate unnecessary duplicate links where appropriate.
Ensure all links lead to the intended destinations.
Preserve logical services, company, resources, and contact groupings.
Ensure menus open and close predictably.
Support keyboard navigation, Escape-key dismissal, logical focus movement, and appropriate focus visibility.
Verify that sticky-header behavior does not hide page headings or anchored content.
Ensure menus remain usable near the page footer.
Test menu opening, closing, scrolling, submenus, language selection, and focus management.
The mobile menu must not extend beyond the viewport or become impossible to scroll.
Inspect every main service category and representative service-detail page.
A specific issue was observed on the Book & Journal Typesetting page around 00:39–00:40 in the screen recording.
The related-service grid appeared visually unbalanced, with remaining cards placed on the left and excessive unused space.
Inspect the actual grid component and resolve the issue if reproducible.
Use a consistent responsive card layout.
Three columns on wide desktop screens.
One column on narrow mobile screens.
Balanced placement when a row contains fewer cards.
Consistent CTA links and hover/focus states.
No unintended empty grid tracks or large layout gaps.
The XML & Structured Content Services card appeared different from neighboring cards. Check whether this is intentional. If not, correct it using the shared card component.
Some service entries, including translation, subtitling, voiceover, and transcription, appeared to link directly to the quote form even though dedicated service-detail pages exist.
Change service-card title/main actions to link to their appropriate detail pages, where confirmed.
Provide a separate quote CTA where useful.
Do not remove valuable service landing pages.
A visible issue was observed around 02:05 in the screen recording.
The floating AI assistant overlapped the rightmost service-selection option in the Get a Quote form.
Prevent the assistant from covering buttons, cards, inputs, dropdowns, notices, or other important content.

text: Inspect fixed positioning, stacking order, responsive offsets, and safe-area insets.
Consider a smaller circular launcher or an alternative position on narrow screens.
Avoid obscuring cookie notices, validation errors, progress indicators, or sticky actions.
Confirm that the launcher and chat panel remain keyboard accessible.
Do not hide or disable the assistant globally unless there is a demonstrated technical or usability need.
Test the assistant on the homepage, contact page, service pages, and every step of the quote form.
Inspect the Work/Portfolio section and all currently published portfolio cards.
The desktop recording showed polished sample presentation, but some titles, such as "Complex 1 typesetting sample", read like internal production labels.
Verify consistent thumbnail sizes and aspect ratios.
Prevent image distortion, poor cropping, and stretched previews.
Make sure cards remain balanced at all screen sizes.
Review current titles and flag internal-looking names for editorial approval.
Do not invent project descriptions or replace approved titles without confirmation.
Ensure public previews use approved assets.
Investigate whether original source documents or confidential material are publicly exposed.
Do not delete or change portfolio publication permissions automatically.
Optimize large images using the existing Next.js image pipeline where appropriate.
Supply responsive sizes and prevent layout shift.
Avoid lazy-loading the main above-the-fold LCP image when it harms performance.
Preserve image quality, especially for publication pages containing small text.
Use authentic approved EPUBTRANS materials when possible.
Do not automatically replace actual portfolio samples with decorative stock images.
